subject: Simulating from a PC matern model

messages.author: 57ef4f99efb73554
messages.subject: Simulating from a PC matern model
parts:
HI, 

I'm currently setting up a simulation study using a PC Matern SPDE. I want to generate samples from both the hyperpriors (tau and kappa) using PC priors and then generate a realisation from an SPDE model. When I run the model (using the same priors), I seem to be getting horribly biased posterior estimates (See tail probabilities attached). I've checked my code multiple times, and I'm not sure where I might be going wrong. Does anyone have any idea what might be going wrong here?

Thanks in advance
Matt

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simulating from a PC matern model
parts:
Hi Matthew,
There's a small but important omission (or at least not very clear issue) in the inla.spde2.pcmatern() documentation: the parameterisation is in theta=(log(rho), log(sigma)), not (log(tau), log(kappa)), so when you simulate your field with the precision from inla.spde.precision() you're getting different parameters than you think, as you use log(tau) and log(kappa) as input, which is incorrect.

As an extra complication, the plain INLA summary output presents the rho and sigma results, and not the log-results, so for any automated analysis, I strongly recommend using the results computed via inla.spde.result(), as that is consistent (nearly, some items are unavailable for pcmatern; will hopefully be obvious from a visual inspection of the output).

Finn
